\title{The Euler Product and the Divergence of the Prime
  Reciprocals\thanks{Written for a test suite; the results are
    Euler's, the exposition is ours.}}
\author{A. Example \and B. Example}
\date{\today}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We prove that the Riemann zeta function factors over the primes for every
real $s > 1$, and we deduce from the factorisation that the sum of the
reciprocals of the primes diverges. The argument needs only absolute
convergence, unique factorisation and the elementary bound
$-\log(1-x) \le x + x^2$ for $0 \le x \le 1/2$.
\end{abstract}
